claims.text: The Llama 3 70B model achieved a mean accuracy of 0.84 in binary classification of coded psychosocial autopsy interview segments.
The Llama 3 70B model achieved substantial agreement with researchers in binary classification with a Cohen's Kappa of 0.68.
The model achieved an accuracy of 0.67 in identifying code segments across entire interview transcripts using a sliding window approach.
Around 80% of the LLM-generated summaries were rated as adequate or good by two independent qualitative researchers.
Unsolicited elaboration occurred in at least 19.7% (247 instances) of the coded segments generated by the model.
The LLM failed to report crucial information under the correct code in 3.0% (38 instances) of the summarized fragments.
Factually wrong or non-existent hallucinated data was present in 1.3% (16 instances) of the model's summarized segments.
The model required approximately 5 hours per interview to perform deductive coding using the sliding window approach.

evidence.description: The model had a mean accuracy of 0.84 (SD: 0.09) in binary classification.
There was substantial agreement with the researcher (Cohens Kappa: 0.68).
The model's accuracy in this task was 0.67.
Eighty percent of the summaries were rated as 'adequate' or 'good' and sufficiently rich for subsequent qualitative analyses.
This occurred in at least 247 of the coded segments (19.7%).
The model failed to summarize crucial information under the correct code in at least 38 instances across the 1,254 fragments (3.0%).
In at least sixteen summarized segments (1.3%), the model fabricated a summary that was factually wrong or based on non-existent data.
The model took approximately 5 h per interview (maximum n = 30,000 words), which was 1 h longer than a researcher typically needed to code the average interview.

methodologies.name: Few-shot LLM deductive coding and summarization pipeline
methodologies.description: Evaluated a server-installed Llama 3 70B Instruct model using few-shot prompts and a sliding window peak detection method to deductively code and summarize semi-structured interview transcripts.
datasets: 38 full-word semi-structured interview transcripts from a railway suicide psychosocial autopsy study
conditions: Few-shot prompt setting (1 positive and 1 negative example)
Sliding window of max 300 words with 75-word sentence step
Peak detection thresholding for segment extraction

limitations.text: Qualitative research is prone to interpretation bias, issues with reproducibility, and high time/labor requirements.
The dataset corpus was not large enough to fine-tune a model with sufficient training and test examples.
The sliding window approach obstructed chronological tracking and context across long interviews.
The evaluation dataset was in Dutch, which may limit generalizability of performance to other languages.
The LLM produced errors including hallucinations, unsolicited elaboration, misinterpretation of pronouns/subjects, and failure to summarize under correct codes.

future_work.text: Replicate findings in different qualitative contexts, subjects, and data structures.
Evaluate models with larger context sizes capable of processing entire interview transcripts without segmentation.
Integrate an active learning loop allowing qualitative researchers to provide direct feedback on coded segments.
